title: Algebra base change realizes module tensor pullback and its unit
statement: Let j:Z→X be any morphism of schemes, a an adjunction tensorPullback j ⊣ pushforward j [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], and B a commutative O_X-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf]. Write U for commAlgebraSheafModule, and F=tensorPullback j ⋙ pushforward j. There exist a commutative O_X-algebra sheaf C, an algebra morphism p:B→C, and an O_X-module isomorphism e:F(U(B))≅U(C), such that U(p)=a.unit.app(U(B));e.hom. No grading, local freeness, closed immersion or coproduct hypothesis is used; e is only a module isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0095 and 0096, inverse image followed by extension of scalars; Tag 09MS, the coefficient quotient on the direct-sum algebra

proof.text: Take the inverse-image algebra sheaf j^{-1}B and extend its scalars to O_Z using the sheafified tensor product of commutative algebras. Push this algebra sheaf forward, using j^sharp for its O_X structure map; call it C. The coefficient map gives an algebra morphism p:B→C.

Forgetting the algebra structure in the inverse-image and scalar-extension construction gives the module inverse image and the sheafified tensor product defining tensorPullback. Both use the same sectionwise tensors, restrictions and scalar actions. Identify the resulting underlying modules by an isomorphism e_0. Under this identification U(p) is the canonical adjunction unit followed by e_0.hom.

For the supplied adjunction a, compare it to the canonical adjunction a_0 using leftAdjointUniq. Compose pushforward of that isomorphism, evaluated at U(B), with e_0 to obtain e. The unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app identity gives U(p)=a.unit.app(U(B));e.hom. This comparison need not preserve algebra multiplication, which is why e is only required to be a module isomorphism. Zero algebras and empty schemes require no exception.
